steps.say: Two Three.js scenes from this week, and both authors credit a model for the code.
This hummingbird's throat flashes violet only when its bill points at you.
This outpost loads no model files at all. Both claims hold, in different ways.

scenes.headline: Seven reposts, read to the source
scenes.sub: A drafter, a reasoning cache, a texture model and two scenes
scenes.say: I'm Gorget. Seven posts went past this week. I read what each one pointed at, starting with that throat.

heads: Every feather is a card with its own platelet normal
A body-wide tint: the same colour from every side
A narrow lobe per feather: only those facing you flash
The power sets how narrow the lobe is
params.wide: low power: a wide, dull sheen
params.narrow: high power: a narrow, bright flash

steps.say: About eleven thousand feathers, each real geometry, each hinged at its root in the vertex shader. And each one carries its own platelet normal.
steps.term: Platelet normal: the direction one feather reflects

steps.say: The README says a body-wide tint never looked right. It shades the whole throat at once.
So the shader lights a narrow lobe around each feather's own normal. The hue slides from maroon to violet as it faces you, and only a few feathers flash at a time.
The brightness is a high power of that alignment. Raise the power and the flash shrinks to a small cone. The README calls it art-directed, not a physical model.
NVIDIA's CPU-ARC starts from a model that has already solved a problem.
A builder reads the transcript and writes Python, with the parts that vary as parameters.
steps.term: Semantic function: code found by its description

steps.say: At run time a fine-tuned one-billion-parameter model only extracts the values. The rest is code on a CPU.
Anything the cache cannot answer falls through to the full model.

states.say: On AIME '25, Opus gets 25 of the 30 problems.
The cache built from those transcripts gets 28. But while it was built, each program was checked against the golden label.

steps.say: MMFlash runs the target twice, with and without the image, and scores each token by how much the image changes its prediction.
steps.caption: Visual dependence: a KL divergence, with and without the image

steps.say: A diffusion drafter accepts 46% of the least image-dependent tokens and 22% of the most. So the loss weights the image-dependent ones up.
For long video, the drafter attends to sinks, strided frames, text and a local window.

scenes.title: Average speedup, Qwen3.5-9B, seven image benchmarks
scenes.say: On Qwen3.5-9B that is 3.05 times on average, against 2.75 for DFlash trained on the same data.

steps.say: UltraTex makes PBR textures from a mesh and one image. First albedo, with shading normals.
Then metallic and roughness, guided by a frozen VLM's middle layers, which know a painted fish from a metal one.
steps.term: PBR: albedo, metallic and roughness maps

steps.say: Roughness error falls to 16.57 from 25.96. Metallic barely moves.

items.say: CPU-ARC's wins over its source are not held out.
UltraTex is Meshy-affiliated, and its code waits on Meshy's review.
And much of the outpost's look comes from its 82 texture maps.

scenes.text: Split a drafter's acceptance by how much the image matters, and you see where it loses.
scenes.say: The idea I would keep: split a drafter's acceptance by how much the image matters, and you see exactly where it loses.

recap: One lobe per feather makes the flash
Cache the solution as code, keep the fallback
Weight the tokens the image decides
scenes.say: One lobe per feather, a cache with a fallback, and a drafter that learns what the image decides.
